title: Separation Anxiety: A Sign of a Strong Bond
hook: When your baby melts down the moment you leave, it's not a setback — it's a normal phase and a sign of healthy attachment. Brief, confident goodbyes and a consistent ritual help.
key_points: Separation anxiety is a normal developmental phase, common from around 9 months through toddlerhood.
It reflects healthy attachment — your child's protest is a sign of the close bond you've built.
Keep goodbyes brief and confident: give a quick, loving send-off, then go, even through the tears.
Consistency and a goodbye ritual (a hug, a phrase, a wave) build trust; always come back when you say you will.
content_html: If your baby clings and cries the instant you step away, take heart: separation anxiety is a normal stage of development, common from around nine months and often continuing into the toddler years. As the AAP puts it, your child's desire to stay with you is a beautiful sign of attachment — proof of the close, secure bond you've built, not evidence that anything is wrong.
extra_html: The most effective approach feels counterintuitive: keep goodbyes short and confident. Give your child your full attention, a loving send-off, and a consistent ritual — a hug, a special phrase, a wave at the window — then leave, even through the protest. Drawing it out tends to make it harder. Doing the same drop-off, at the same time, the same way builds predictability and trust, and it helps to always come back when you say you will. Practicing short separations with a trusted caregiver beforehand can ease the transition too. This is general educational information from the AAP — if anxiety seems extreme or persists well beyond the preschool years, check in with your pediatrician.

source.name: HealthyChildren.org (AAP) — How to Ease Your Child's Separation Anxiety

related.title: Why Toddlers Have Tantrums
related.hook: Tantrums are a normal part of toddler development — big feelings hitting a brain that can't yet manage them or fully put them into words.

related.title: Soothing a Fussy Newborn
related.hook: Newborns are wired to be calmed by sensations that echo the womb — holding, swaddling, gentle motion, white noise, and sucking. One rule overrides all: never, ever shake a baby.

related.title: Stranger Anxiety: A New Kind of Wary
related.hook: Around 6 to 9 months, a once-sociable baby may suddenly turn shy or cry around unfamiliar people — even doting grandparents. It's a normal sign their mind and memory are growing.

flashcards.prompt: What does separation anxiety usually signal?

choices.text: A normal phase and a sign of healthy attachment
That the child is spoiled or being manipulative
A developmental problem that needs treatment

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP describes separation anxiety as normal and a sign of a meaningful, healthy attachment between child and caregiver.

flashcards.prompt: What goodbye approach does the AAP recommend?
flashcards.back_html: Keep it brief and confident — give a quick, loving send-off using a consistent ritual (a hug, a phrase, a wave), then go, even if your child cries. Always return when you promise.
